newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister says elections a last resort.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister says elections a last resort.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Abdullah Gul said on Wednesday his Islamist wing of government was prepared to call elections as a last resort but was reluctant to do so for fear of harming the economy.
"My party is ready for this but for the economy it is not profitable," Gul said in an interview with Reuters when asked about the likelihood of fresh elections.

"There is a time for this, of course. It is the last recourse...If we believe that all other ways are blocked then in a democratic country you have to go to the people and get their opinion again," Gul said.
But he added: "Since we are in government, we are accountable and we should act responsibly."
Turkey's military-dominated National Security Council has demanded the coalition crack down on a rise in Islam-based activism since it came to power last June.
The call has raised tensions between Islamists and the secular establishment and strained the government alliance.

One of the military demands -- to raise compulsory state education to eight years from five -- has provoked opposition from Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party, which sees the measure as a threat to the role of religious schools.
